title: Core parking bench
intro: Reproduce the measurements behind the RigPolice article https://rigpolice.com/system/articles/disable-cpu-core-parking/ . `parking-bench.ps1` has three tests. `burst` (the default) releases one thread per logical CPU after an idle pause and records the work done in each 1 ms window, the test where parked cores show. `framesim` runs a synthetic frame loop. `game` captures the frame times of a running load. Every test records the parked-core count. The CS2 load below is the CPU-bound real-game check.
needs: Run one power state per series: stock, then each state you want to compare (for example after `cpu-parking-disabler.ps1`).
run: `.\parking-bench.ps1 -Phase stock` (burst), `.\parking-bench.ps1 -Phase stock -Test framesim`, `.\parking-bench.ps1 -Phase stock -Test game -Load cs2 -PresentMon <path to PresentMon-2.6.0-x64.exe>`; then the same with `-Phase tweaked`. For a capped game run add `-FpsMax <N>` to the game command (for example `-FpsMax 144`; see the section below). Results go next to the script, or to `-OutDir`.
touch: only its own worker threads, a performance counter query, an ETW session named `rigpolice-ppm` (provider `Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-Processor-Power`, keyword `0x44`) that it starts and stops itself around every test, writing a temporary ETL file that it deletes after decoding it, and, for `-Test game`, PresentMon with its own ETW session named `rigpolice-bench`. It writes a one-time calibration file `parking-bench-config.json` next to the script and reads the game log named in the recipe. With `-FpsMax` it also presses one key (F9) into CS2, only while CS2 is the foreground window. The key runs the bind you typed. CS2 keeps that bind, and on every game run of the CS2 map it saves `fps_max` in its own config files when it exits (undo: the **Undo** paragraph under Steps)
game:
For `-Test game` start the bench before the load: it waits for the load's process and, when the recipe names a start line, for that line in the game log, then waits the load pause and captures. Do not touch the PC until it prints the result.

**Capped run (`-FpsMax <N>`, CS2 only).** Before the console line, type this into the CS2 console and press Enter (the bench prints it with your N filled in):

```
bind F9 "echo rigpolice_cap_key; fps_max <N>"
```

Then type the console line as usual. The map resets `fps_max` when it loads and again after the start line, when the game log shows `Cannot set convar 'fps_max'`. After that line the bench presses F9 once, only while CS2 is the foreground window; if it is not, the run fails. The load pause is still counted from the start line, so a capped and an uncapped run capture the same part of the route. The bench refuses an N whose period, 1000 / N ms, is within 3% of the refresh period of your monitor, and rejects the run when the median frame time is not within 2% of 1000 / N ms.

**Undo.** Every game run of the CS2 map changes `fps_max`: the map sets it to 0, and a capped run then sets it to N. CS2 saves the last value when it exits, and a capped run also leaves F9 bound. Before your first CS2 game run, note what `fps_max` and `bind F9` print in the CS2 console. Afterwards type `fps_max <noted value>`, then `bind F9 "<noted command>"`, or `unbind F9` if F9 was unbound.
record: `parking-bench.ps1` adds the parked-core count, the power state at the end of the run (a change marks the run) and, for `-Test game`, the game build, whether the installed video config matches the shipped one (mismatched key names only) and the names of launch flags outside the recipe (names only, no values), and the count of frames PresentMon lost to a present event buffer overflow (`presentMon.overflowedPresents`; a run that lost any is rejected). Every result also holds a `ppm` object for the measured part of the run (the burst, the frame loop or the capture): `session` and `keyword` of the `rigpolice-ppm` trace; `startedBeforeLoad`, whether the trace started before the load process existed (game runs; null otherwise); `buffersLost`, taken from `logman query` and null when its output has no `Buffers Lost` line (logman prints localized labels on some Windows languages); `profileChanges`, every processor power profile change the trace saw, as profile ids with the offset in seconds from the start of the measured part (zero or negative means before it); `captureProfile`, the profile id in effect when the measured part started, null when the trace saw no change before it or a change fell inside it; and `captureChanges`, the number of changes inside it. The trace logs only changes, so an empty list means no change was seen. Profile ids are recorded as numbers only. For `-Test game` the result also holds `autoGameModeEnabled`, the value of `AutoGameModeEnabled` under `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\GameBar` read before the capture (null when it does not exist), and `cap`, null on an uncapped run and otherwise `fpsMax`, `periodMs` (1000 / `fpsMax`), `tolerance`, `slowFrameFactor`, `slowFrames` (frames longer than `slowFrameFactor` times the period), `pressedAfterStartSeconds` (seconds from the start line to the key press) and `echoSeen` (whether the bind's echo text appeared in the game log after the press; it is recorded and never rejects a run).
